records.title: openrisc: Add text patching API support
records.body:
Add text patching api's to use in subsequent jump_label implementation.  We use
a new fixmap FIX_TEXT_POKE0 entry to temporarily override MMU mappings to allow
read only text pages to be written to.

Previously, __set_fix was marked with __init as it was only used during the
EARLYCON stage. Now that TEXT_POKE mappings require post-init usage
(e.g., FIX_TEXT_POKE0), keeping __init would cause runtime bugs whenset_fixmap
accesses invalid memory. Thus, we remove the __init flag to ensure __set_fix
remains valid beyond initialization.

A new function patch_insn_write is exposed to allow single instruction patching.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/openrisc/aJIC8o1WmVHol9RY@antec/T/#t

Signed-off-by: chenmiao <chenmiao.ku@gmail.com>

records.body:
Supported a complete jump_label implementation based on the ARM64 and
RV64 version and add the CONFIG_JUMP_LABEL=y to the defconfig.

Testing was conducted using a dedicated test module jump-label-test,
provided in the link below. For detailed steps, please refer to the
README also at the provided link.

Link: https://github.com/ChenMiaoi/GSoC-2025-Final-Report/tree/main/tests/jump-label-test

Test Environment:
  - Hardware: QEMU emulated OR1K
  - Kernel Version: 6.17.0-rc3-dirty
  - Configs: CONFIG_MODULES=y,CONFIG_MODULE_UNLOAD=y
  - Toolchain: or1k-none-linux-musl-gcc 15.1.0

Test Results:
$ insmod jump_label_test.ko
[   32.590000] Jump label performance test module loaded
[   35.250000] Normal branch time: 1241327150 ns (124 ns per iteration)
[   35.250000] Jump label (false) time: 706422700 ns (70 ns per iteration)
[   35.250000] Jump label (true) time: 708913450 ns (70 ns per iteration)
$ rmmod jump_label_test.ko
[   72.210000] Jump label test module unloaded

The results show approximately 43% improvement in branch performance
when using jump labels compared to traditional branches.

+/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only */
+/*
+ * Copyright (C) 2025 Chen Miao
+ *
+ * Based on arch/arm/include/asm/jump_label.h
+ */
+#ifndef __ASM_OPENRISC_JUMP_LABEL_H
+#define __ASM_OPENRISC_JUMP_LABEL_H
+
+#ifndef __ASSEMBLER__
+
+#include <linux/types.h>
+#include <asm/insn-def.h>
+
+#define HAVE_JUMP_LABEL_BATCH
+
+#define JUMP_LABEL_NOP_SIZE OPENRISC_INSN_SIZE
+
+/**
+ * JUMP_TABLE_ENTRY - Create a jump table entry
+ * @key: Jump key identifier (typically a symbol address)
+ * @label: Target label address
+ *
+ * This macro creates a jump table entry in the dedicated kernel section (__jump_table).
+ * Each entry contains the following information:
+ * 		Offset from current instruction to jump instruction (1b - .)
+ * 		Offset from current instruction to target label (label - .)
+ * 		Offset from current instruction to key identifier (key - .)
+ */
+#define JUMP_TABLE_ENTRY(key, label)			\
+	".pushsection	__jump_table, \"aw\"	\n\t"	\
+	".align 	4 			\n\t"	\
+	".long 		1b - ., " label " - .	\n\t"	\
+	".long 		" key " - . 		\n\t"	\
+	".popsection				\n\t"
+
+#define ARCH_STATIC_BRANCH_ASM(key, label)		\
+	".align		4			\n\t"	\
+	"1: l.nop				\n\t"	\
+	"    l.nop				\n\t"	\
+	JUMP_TABLE_ENTRY(key, label)
+
+static __always_inline bool arch_static_branch(struct static_key *const key,
+					       const bool branch)
+{
+	asm goto (ARCH_STATIC_BRANCH_ASM("%0", "%l[l_yes]")
+		  ::"i"(&((char *)key)[branch])::l_yes);
+
+	return false;
+l_yes:
+	return true;
+}
+
+#define ARCH_STATIC_BRANCH_JUMP_ASM(key, label)		\
+	".align		4			\n\t"	\
+	"1: l.j	" label "			\n\t"	\
+	"    l.nop				\n\t"	\
+	JUMP_TABLE_ENTRY(key, label)
+
+static __always_inline bool
+arch_static_branch_jump(struct static_key *const key, const bool branch)
+{
+	asm goto (ARCH_STATIC_BRANCH_JUMP_ASM("%0", "%l[l_yes]")
+		  ::"i"(&((char *)key)[branch])::l_yes);
+
+	return false;
+l_yes:
+	return true;
+}
+
+#endif /* __ASSEMBLER__ */
+#endif /* __ASM_OPENRISC_JUMP_LABEL_H */

records.body:
Adds a public `getOpcodeStr()` member function to `UnaryOperator`, mirroring the same-named method already present on `BinaryOperator`. It simply forwards to the existing static `UnaryOperator::getOpcodeStr(Opcode)`.

No functional change. The underlying static function is already exercised by existing tests, so no new unit tests are added.

records.title: [clang] Fix crashes and error recovery for nested pragmas
records.body:
Nested `_Pragma` or Microsoft `__pragma` expressions can produce annotation tokens in an enclosing pragma's arguments. This patch fixes crashes when these tokens are processed as arguments or used to construct diagnostics, and improves error recovery for nested pragmas.

**Calling `getIdentifierInfo()` on annotations in expanded or buffered arguments**

```cc
#pragma vtordisp(push, _Pragma("weak foobar"))
```

After the inner `_Pragma` is processed, the enclosing pragma receives an annotation where it expects a mode argument. Similar cases occur when arguments are buffered and parsed later.

Previously, these paths called `getIdentifierInfo()` and then checked whether the result was null. The assertion occurs inside the getter, so checking its return value cannot prevent the crash.

This patch checks the token kind before calling the getter. Only `identifiers` or `keywords` permitted by the pragma's syntax are queried for identifier information; other tokens follow the existing diagnostic and recovery paths.

**Calling `getSpelling()` on annotations in diagnostics or message construction**

Some handlers already check the argument's token kind, but still call `getSpelling()` when reporting an invalid argument. Annotation tokens do not have an ordinary source spelling that this interface can read, so constructing the diagnostic can itself cause a crash.

This patch skips spelling lookup for annotation tokens and omits the argument spelling and its surrounding quotes from the diagnostic. For example:

```cc
#pragma clang optimize _Pragma("weak foobar") on
```

Clang now reports:

```text
error: unexpected argument to '#pragma clang optimize'; expected 'on' or 'off'
```

Message construction for `#pragma GCC dependency` also skips annotations while preserving ordinary tokens. For example, when the dependency is newer than the source file:

```cc
#pragma GCC dependency "header.h" before _Pragma("weak foobar") after
```

With this patch, Clang reports:

```text
warning: current file is older than dependency before foobar after
```

Ordinary invalid arguments retain their spelling in diagnostics. For example, an argument of `42` is still displayed as `'42'`.

**Unexpanded token reads can still return annotations after `__pragma` captures its arguments**

```cc
__pragma(clang __debug macro _Pragma("weak foobar"))
```

Although these paths use `LexUnexpandedToken()`, `__pragma` expands and captures its arguments before passing them to the handler. The inner `_Pragma` has already been processed, so an unexpanded read can still return an annotation.

This patch adds token-kind checks in namespace dispatch and the affected handlers. Dispatch continues to use the original name stored in `IdentifierInfo`, preserving keyword aliases.

**Nested pragma terminators and error recovery**

```cc
#pragma vtordisp(_Pragma("clang __debug dump x"))
int after;
int use(void) { return after; }
```

The `clang __debug dump` handler injects an annotation and leaves its arguments and `eod` for the parser. When the enclosing handler discards invalid arguments, it can mistake this inner `eod` for its own end marker, leaving the remaining `)` to the parser and disrupting subsequent declarations.

This patch records lexer boundaries while processing pragmas and capturing `__pragma` arguments. It skips only `eod` tokens from deeper pragma lexers. End markers in ordinary replay streams remain intact, including those used for `-E` output.

The boundaries are also updated when a macro lexer is popped, handling pragmas that start within a macro expansion and finish outside it.

Handlers that consume annotation arguments directly explicitly discard the remaining directive. Microsoft pragmas whose arguments are buffered for later parsing continue to use the existing cleanup logic.

**Independent crash in `__pragma(mark ...)`**

``__pragma(mark foo)`` can crash without annotation tokens because the mark handler assumes a character lexer is available. When processing a captured token stream without a character lexer, the handler now consumes the remaining arguments and ignores the mark.

Fixes #225035

comments.body:
@epage @AlexTMjugador I think `build.warnings` should have consistent semantics across human-readable and JSON output. `--message-format` should only change how messages are represented, not how warnings are handled.

Specifically, I would lean toward:
- `allow`: Filter out lint warning diagnostics, including the corresponding JSON messages, without failing the build or emitting an additional notice.
- `warn` (the default): Preserve lint warning diagnostics without failing the build because of them.
- `deny`: Preserve lint warning diagnostics, but fail the build and explain why, without changing the original diagnostics to `error`.

As for `-D warnings`, my understanding is that it promotes the relevant lint diagnostics to errors within Clippy, so they would remain visible even with `build.warnings = "allow"`. Downstream tools could still consume those errors, for example to generate SARIF. This would, however, filter out diagnostics that remain at the warning level when `allow` is set, which I think is consistent with the user explicitly choosing to suppress lint warnings.

records.title: [clang][Sema] Fix crash caused by invalid implicit format attributes
records.body:
Clang implicitly adds `format_arg(1)` to `__CFStringMakeConstantString`, including prototypeless declarations created during error recovery. A zero-argument call can then cause format string checking to access a nonexistent argument and crash.

Reproducer:

```c
void a(char *) __attribute__((format(__CFString__, 1, 2)));
void b() { a(__CFStringMakeConstantString()); }
```

Before this change, an assertions-enabled build crashes after reporting the source errors (diagnostic excerpts):

```text
error: call to undeclared function '__CFStringMakeConstantString';
       ISO C99 and later do not support implicit function declarations
error: incompatible integer to pointer conversion passing 'int' to parameter of type 'char *'
Assertion `Arg < getNumArgs() && "Arg access out of range!"' failed.
```

In `Sema::AddKnownFunctionAttributes()`, check that the function type is a prototype function type and that the referenced format string parameter exists before implicitly adding `format` or `format_arg` attributes.

Fixes #225034

records.title: [libc][math] Prevent spurious floating-point exceptions in fdim
records.body:
Without `FENV_ACCESS` enabled, Clang at `-O2` optimizes the conditional expression in `fdim`:

```cpp
return x > y ? x - y : T(0);
```

into the following LLVM IR:

```llvm
%cmp = fcmp ogt double %x, %y
%diff = fsub double %x, %y
%result = select i1 %cmp, double %diff, double 0.000000e+00
```

The `fsub` is not guarded by `x > y`. Even when `x <= y`, the subtraction executes before `select` chooses zero as the result. The `select` only chooses a value; it cannot undo floating-point exceptions already raised by the subtraction. Consequently, `fdim(-inf, -inf)` raises `FE_INVALID`, `fdim(-max, -min_subnormal)` raises `FE_INEXACT`, and `fdim(-max, max)` can raise `FE_OVERFLOW` and `FE_INEXACT`, despite all these calls returning zero.

Without floating-point environment access enabled, the compiler need not preserve the observable behavior of these exceptions and can speculate the subtraction. Simply rewriting the conditional expression as an `if` statement does not reliably prevent this optimization.

Enable `FENV_ACCESS` in the shared implementation so the subtraction uses `llvm.experimental.constrained.fsub` with dynamic rounding and strict exception semantics. The optimized IR keeps the subtraction in the `x > y` branch, avoiding spurious exceptions on the path that returns zero. Enable `FENV_ACCESS` in the public entry points as well to allow the strict floating-point implementation to be inlined.

Fixes #88771

This version appears to work without optimization, but at `-O2` and `-O3`, Clang still emits an unconditional subtraction, as shown here:

https://godbolt.org/z/TY53Gdx46

``` asm
movaps  xmm2, xmm0
subss   xmm2, xmm1
cmpnless        xmm0, xmm1
```

I initially considered this approach too, but the original issue also notes that "replacing the conditional operator with an `if-statement` is brittle and can still produce the same problematic assembly".

So I don’t think switching to an `if-statement` alone is a reliable fix, and I believe we still need `LIBC_FENV_ACCESS_ON` on targets that support it.

comments.body:
@lntue 

Hi, I looked into the currently failing tests, and the `armhf` test failure under QEMU appears to be related to `LIBC_FENV_ACCESS_ON` not taking effect.

After reproducing this locally, I found that `#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON` is not supported by the Clang version and `armhf` target configuration I tested. Here is a simplified reproducer comparing code generation with `FENV_ACCESS` enabled and disabled:

https://godbolt.org/z/jfEEWx8Gz

``` asm
// some assembly instructions omitted
vsub.f32   s4, s0, s1
vmovgt.f32 s2, s4
```

In this example, both versions generate the same key instructions: the floating-point subtraction `x - y` is performed unconditionally, and the comparison result then determines whether its result is used. Therefore, even when `x > y` is false and the function ultimately returns zero, the subtraction may already have raised a floating-point exception. This explains why the current fix does not resolve the test failure in this configuration.

Should this PR use a different implementation in libc to avoid this unnecessary floating-point operation? Or does this require improving Clang’s support for `FENV_ACCESS` on this ARM target before addressing the test failure?

One more question: if we decide to add support for `FENV_ACCESS` on armhf, should I open a separate issue and address it in a separate PR, or include that work in this PR?

records.title: [libc] Fix missing Annex K declarations caused by header include order
records.body:
If `__STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__` is defined as `1` after including `stdio.h`, a subsequent inclusion of `string.h` does not expose the declaration of `strnlen_s`. `stdio.h` indirectly includes `annex-k-macros.h` through shared type headers. This header sets its include guard even when Annex K is disabled, preventing later inclusions from checking the request macro again.

Remove the include guard from `annex-k-macros.h` so each inclusion can re-evaluate the Annex K enablement condition. Guard the definition of `LIBC_HAS_ANNEX_K` separately to avoid redefining it.

Also move the include guard definitions in `errno_t.h`, `rsize_t.h`, and `constraint_handler_t.h` into their Annex K conditional blocks. This prevents an initial inclusion with Annex K disabled from blocking subsequent type definitions.

Fixes #195276

records.title: [libc] Request for Annex K via `__STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__` doesn't work as expected
records.body:
Source code:
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#define __STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__ 1
#include <string.h>

int foo() {
  return strnlen_s("abc", 2);
}
```
Compile with:
`clang -c a.c`

We get the error:
```
a.c:6:10: error: call to undeclared function 'strnlen_s'; ISO C99 and later do not support implicit function declarations [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]
    6 |   return strnlen_s("abc", 2);
      |          ^
```

If we move the line `#define __STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__ 1` before `#include <stdio.h>`, it works as expected.

**Analysis**

I believe this issue is caused by the header inclusion guard in `llvm-libc-macros/annex-k-macros.h`.

The inclusion of `stdio.h` implies a recursive inclusion of `annex-k-macros.h`. But at that point, the `__STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__` is not yet defined, therefore the macro who controls the availability of Annex K functionality, `LIBC_HAS_ANNEX_K`, is not defined.

By the time `__STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__` is defined and `string.h` is included, the recursive inclusion of `annex-k-macros.h` (by the second time now) is stopped at the header inclusion guard, hence `LIBC_HAS_ANNEX_K` is again not defined. As a result, the declaration of `strnlen_s` is never brought in.

records.body:
Calls such as the following fail because the preprocessor treats the comma in the initializer as a macro argument separator:

``` c
struct PairUI { unsigned int first, second; };
stdc_count_ones((struct PairUI){ 2U, 3U }.first);
```

Use variadic macros so `__VA_ARGS__` preserves all argument tokens, including the separating commas, reconstructing the original expression.

Fixes #81503.

comments.body:
I reproduced the issue locally. While working on a fix, I put together the following test:

1. https://godbolt.org/z/nYY41P38G
2. https://godbolt.org/z/GcoKK7Eqs
3. https://godbolt.org/z/heW44dPY3

``` cc
extern "C" void* resolver() {
  return nullptr;
}

[[gnu::weak, gnu::ifunc("resolver")]] void selector();  // first, GCC error, Clang ok

void selector(void) __attribute__((ifunc("resolver"))); // second, GCC ok, Clang ok

[[gnu::ifunc("resolver")]]void selector(void); // third, GCC ok, Clang ok

#pragma weak selector

```

Of the three cases, **GCC diagnoses the first but accepts the second and third, while Clang accepts all three**.

I compiled each of the three test cases separately on my local machine and inspected the resulting object-file symbols. The results are as follows:

``` text
OS: Fedora Linux 44
Clang: clang version 22.1.8 (Fedora 22.1.8-4.fc44)
GCC: gcc version 16.2.1 20260819 (Red Hat 16.2.1-2)
```

| Test case | Clang | GCC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| first | Strong IFUNC; weak is not preserved | Error; no object file produced |
| second | Strong IFUNC | Weak IFUNC |
| third| Strong IFUNC | Weak IFUNC |

In the versions and configuration I tested, Clang silently ignores weak in all three cases, whereas GCC rejects the explicit combination but emits a **`weak IFUNC`** in the two cases using `#pragma weak`.

As far as I understand, `ISO C/C++` does not specify how weak and ifunc should interact. **However, the [GCC documentation](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-15.2.0/gcc/Common-Function-Attributes.html#index-ifunc-function-attribute) states that “Indirect functions cannot be weak,” and the [Clang documentation](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AttributeReference.html#ifunc) states that “The entity must not have weak linkage.”**

Based on these documented restrictions, should the second and third cases also be rejected? In other words, **is the restriction on the resulting entity’s linkage, regardless of how it is specified?** If so, an `IFUNC` with `weak` linkage should be rejected even when the attributes are introduced through separate declarations or the weak linkage is introduced via `#pragma weak`.

records.title: [clang] Reject enum element types in ext_vector_type
records.body:
`BuildExtVectorType` checks element types with `isIntegerType()`, which also accepts complete unscoped enums. However,
`ASTContext::getExtVectorType` does not support enum elements.

For example:

```c
typedef enum { A } E;
typedef E V __attribute__((ext_vector_type(4)));
```

Before this change, compiling with `-fsyntax-only` in an assertion-enabled build crashes in `ASTContext::getExtVectorType`:

```text
QualType clang::ASTContext::getExtVectorType(QualType, unsigned int) const:
Assertion `vecType->isBuiltinType() || vecType->isDependentType() ||
(vecType->isBitIntType() && llvm::isPowerOf2_32(vecType->castAs<BitIntType>()->getNumBits()))' failed.
```

Explicitly reject enum element types in `BuildExtVectorType` so that the same code produces a diagnostic instead:

```text
error: invalid vector element type 'E'
```

records.title: [clang] Fix crash on unterminated __identifier
records.body:
With Microsoft extensions enabled, e.g. via `-fms-compatibility`, the following input triggers an assertion:

```cpp
# 1 __identifier(foo
```

The `__identifier` handler consumes the end-of-directive token, `eod`, while looking for `)`, but still returns `foo` to the line-marker handler. The latter rejects `foo` as an invalid filename and tries to discard the remaining tokens up to the end of the directive. Since `eod` has already been consumed, it encounters `eof` and triggers an assertion.

Return `eod`, `eof`, and `annotation` tokens to the caller when recovering from a missing `)`.

Fixes #222310

records.title: [clang][Sema] Check swift_attr argument count in type contexts
records.body:
`HandleSwiftAttr` checks the first argument with
`checkStringLiteralArgumentAttr` without validating the argument count. Unlike declaration attributes, this path does not go through `checkCommonAttributeFeatures`, so a missing argument causes an out-of-bounds access in `ParsedAttr::getArg`.

For example:

```c
int * __attribute__((__swift_attr__)) a;
```

Before this change, compiling this code crashes. In assertion-enabled builds, it fails in `ParsedAttr::getArg` with:

```text
Assertion `Arg < NumArgs && "Arg access out of range!"' failed.
```

Check that the attribute has exactly one argument in `HandleSwiftAttr` before reading it so that the same code produces a diagnostic instead:

```text
error: '__swift_attr__' attribute takes one argument
```

Fixes #227549

records.body:
Clang previously accepted both `weak` and `ifunc` attributes on the same
function, but silently ignored `weak` when emitting the IFUNC. Since
`ifunc` functions must not have weak linkage, the new mutual exclusion
rule diagnoses the conflict during attribute processing and
redeclaration merging.

records.title: [clang] Fix crash on unterminated __identifier (#229156)
records.body:
With Microsoft extensions enabled, e.g. via `-fms-compatibility`, the
following input triggers an assertion:

```cpp
# 1 __identifier(foo
```

The `__identifier` handler consumes the end-of-directive token, `eod`,
while looking for `)`, but still returns `foo` to the line-marker
handler. The latter rejects `foo` as an invalid filename and tries to
discard the remaining tokens up to the end of the directive. Since `eod`
has already been consumed, it encounters `eof` and triggers an
assertion.

Return `eod`, `eof`, and `annotation` tokens to the caller when
recovering from a missing `)`.
